items.mainDefect: Salesforce getClient fetches and persists a fresh access token but builds the jsforce Connection with the stale stored access_token.

secondary.defect: The Salesforce token refresh runs on every service instantiation with no expiry check, so every calendar operation makes an extra HTTP call and DB write.

items.mainDefect: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys both evaluate to "[object Object]" and collide, so the schema validates only access_token and none of the intended expiry/other fields.

secondary.defect: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the literal placeholder "refresh_token" when refresh_token is missing, and office365calendar persists it over the real refresh token.

items.mainDefect: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys both evaluate to "[object Object]" and collide, so the expiry mapping doesn't exist and z.object strips all other token fields.

secondary.defect: The placeholder string "refresh_token" is injected for a missing refresh_token, and office365calendar persists it over the real refresh token, which corrupts the credential.

items.mainDefect: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys collide as "[object Object]", so the schema is effectively only access_token and strips all other credential fields.

secondary.defect: parseRefreshTokenResponse fabricates refresh_token = "refresh_token", which consumers such as office365calendar and zoom persist over the real stored token.

items.mainDefect: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys collide as "[object Object]", so the expiry check is lost and z.object strips refresh_token, expiry_date, instance_url and other fields.

secondary.defect: Lines 25-27 assign the literal "refresh_token" to a missing refresh_token, and office365calendar persists it over the real Microsoft refresh token.

items.mainDefect: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys collide as "[object Object]", so only access_token survives parsing and the expiry from the sync endpoint is dropped.

secondary.defect: Because refresh_token is always stripped, the code at lines 25-27 always inserts the "refresh_token" placeholder.

items.mainDefect: Salesforce's new eager token refresh blocks every operation and throws on any token-endpoint failure, so all Salesforce calendar operations fail instead of using the stored credentials.

secondary.defect: salesforceTokenSchema requires scope, which Salesforce's refresh_token grant response does not reliably include, so validation fails.
The success check compares response.statusText to "OK" instead of using response.ok.

items.mainDefect: The app-credential webhook has no req.method check, so a GET/HEAD with a valid secret hits schema.parse(undefined) and returns an unhandled 500.

secondary.defect: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws unhandled on malformed ciphertext or a wrong encryption key instead of returning a 400.
The decrypted keys are persisted as credential.key without checking that they are an object.
The findFirst-then-update/create sequence is not atomic, so concurrent sync calls can create duplicate credentials for the same user and app.
